claim: L7 (LFP-primary analysis spec): trial-by-trial band-power correlation across area x layer nodes, stim and omission computed separately, node x node correlation matrix per band per condition + difference matrix, FDR-corrected significance.
supersedes: An earlier version of this evidence node (same date, same file) characterized the only real-data bug found as a figure-layout issue. That was INCOMPLETE -- a second, more consequential bug (silent node-key collision causing data loss) was found afterward during L8 development and is documented fully below. This version replaces that earlier, incomplete account.
implementation: context/figures/L7_cross_area_power_correlation/L7_cross_area_power_correlation.py. Reuses L3's precomputed-TFR-array + channel_layers_all.csv node infrastructure (load_tfr equivalent, sup/deep channel masks) rather than rebuilding. Per-trial log-last dB (channels-in-node pooled linear, band pooled linear, divided by that TRIAL's own baseline power, log10 once) -- a per-trial normalization, not an average of dB values across trials. Pearson r computed within one session/condition at a time, never pooled or trial-concatenated across sessions, per omission-statistics 'test within session first'. BH-FDR (jnwb.StatisticalAnalysis.fdr_correct) applied once across the full flattened node-pair x band family per session/condition, alpha=0.05, per omission-statistics 'flatten the whole grid, correct once'.
self_test: 4 synthetic nodes, known trial-level structure: n1-n2 strongly correlated both conditions (recovered r=0.73/0.75, FDR q<0.05 in stim) -- PASS. n3-n4 independent both conditions (r=-0.06/-0.07, correctly NOT significant, q=0.49>=0.05) -- PASS. n1-n3 correlated ONLY in synthetic omission (stim r=-0.06, omission r=0.61, recovered difference +0.68) -- PASS, difference matrix recovers the known condition-specific coupling. Mismatched-trial-count pair-exclusion guard and determinism check also PASS. Rerun and reconfirmed passing after the node-key fix below (fix did not touch this self-test's synthetic-node code path).
bug_1_node_key_data_loss: The original node key was a bare f'{area}{layer}'. sub-V182o_ses-260702 genuinely records FEF on TWO DIFFERENT PROBES (A and B). node_trial_traces built a dict keyed by this bare string (out[node_key] = band_traces), so the second probe's FEF data silently OVERWROTE the first's -- not a labeling ambiguity, an actual loss of one probe's data with no error or warning. First real run reported only 4 nodes for this session (FEFdeep, FEFsup, MTdeep, MTsup) when 6 existed. Found during L8 development when the same latent pattern produced a visible label collision there (L8 doesn't use a dict, so it showed up as duplicate labels rather than silent loss -- see L8's evidence node). Fixed by making every node key probe-qualified (f'{area}{layer}_{probe}'), always, not conditionally. Rerun: sub-V182o_ses-260702 now correctly shows 6 nodes (FEFdeep_A, FEFdeep_B, FEFsup_A, FEFsup_B, MTdeep_C, MTsup_C) and its correlation matrix and significant-pair counts changed materially from the pre-fix run (see real_run below) -- a genuine correctness fix, not cosmetic.
bug_2_figure_layout: First real-data render mis-placed the 'Pearson r (stim)' colorbar (overlapped session row 2's node labels) and clipped the suptitle at the canvas top -- caught on the required visual-inspection gate (omission-figures skill: 'export without looking is not verification'). Root cause: fig.colorbar(..., ax=axes[:, :-1]) with a 2D axes array does not lay out predictably across dissimilar-sized per-row matrices. Fixed with explicit GridSpec columns for both colorbars plus fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.90); re-rendered and re-verified visually.

real_run.runtime: 4m48s initial + 34s layout-fix rerun (numbers unchanged) + 5m22s node-key-fix rerun (numbers CHANGED for sub-V182o_ses-260702, see bug_1 above)
sessions_final: sub-V182o_ses-260702 (6 nodes: FEF sup+deep on BOTH probe A and probe B, plus MT sup+deep -- corrected from the pre-fix 4-node run)
real_run.caveat_single_subject: All 3 qualifying sessions (top-3 by node coverage) happen to be V182o -- a single-subject result for this run, stated because it was not planned, not a deliberate restriction.
real_run.finding_1: FEFdeep-FEFsup WITHIN one probe (same-probe, adjacent depth) shows a consistently near-1 trial-level power correlation in every session, every band, both conditions -- the same same-probe-adjacent-depth pattern L6 (volume-conduction control) and L8 (cross-area coherence) also independently flag as often reference-driven.
real_run.finding_2_new_since_fix: On sub-V182o_ses-260702, FEF recorded on probe A is ALSO strongly trial-power-correlated with FEF recorded on probe B (a uniformly high 4x4 block across FEFdeep_A/FEFsup_A/FEFdeep_B/FEFsup_B, all bands) -- invisible in the pre-fix 4-node run since one probe's data was silently absent. Read against L8: for this SAME session/pair, L8's cross-area coherence found FEF-A<->FEF-B standard coherence LOW (0.08-0.13) with low imaginary coherency too -- the two statistics disagree on how 'coupled' these are. Not resolved here (trial-power correlation and phase coherence measure different things -- a shared slow arousal/state signal can drive correlated power without phase-locked activity) -- flagged as a cross-metric discrepancy for the manuscript text, not smoothed over.
real_run.finding_3: sub-V182o_ses-260715 is an outlier: 13-15 of 15 node pairs FDR-significant in every band and both conditions, completely non-selective across frequency and area -- more consistent with a session-wide shared artifact than genuine area-specific coupling. L8 independently flags elevated (not saturated) cross-probe PFC<->FEF coherence for this same session -- a cross-validating signal. sub-V182o_ses-260702 (post-fix) is now also fairly dense (7-9/15 across bands). sub-V182o_ses-260629 is the sparsest (3-9/15).
real_run.reported_honestly: None of these findings is spun into a claim about real inter-area coupling -- reported as observations requiring caution and cross-metric reconciliation, per CLAUDE.md tripwire 10 and the spec's own 'do not conclude' instruction (0.8).

not_yet_done: Difference matrix (omission-stim) has no independent FDR correction -- no resampling null built for the difference itself, stated explicitly in stats JSON, not silently implied significant. Only 3 sessions qualified given the corpus's real node-coverage limits; no cross-session pooling attempted (per corpus discipline, would need the shuffle-null-then-proportion design from omission-signal S10 to be valid, not built here). The L7-vs-L8 discrepancy on FEF-A/FEF-B coupling (trial-power correlation high, coherence low) is flagged but not investigated further -- a stated open question, not a resolved one.
